label: Diagram 15.2
caption: Diagram 15.2 Relationship between building and hardstanding/access roads for high reach fire appliances
description: The drawing is a diagram, with a table beneath it. At top left it reads "See paras 15.8 and 15.9". A grey building mass with a pitched-roof outline occupies the left, with a small projecting block on its right side; to the right of the building the text "Face of building at ground level or vertical plane of projecting upper storey" identifies its right-hand face. Two horizontal green dimension lines with arrowheads run from this face to the right; the upper line is divided into a and b, the lower into c and d, where a spans from the face to the near edge of the hardstanding, b the width of the hardstanding, c the distance from the face to the further edge, and d the gap to a small grey block labelled "Obstruction". A grey band below is labelled "Hardstanding or access road". A dashed outline, open at the bottom, at top right contains the text "Overhead obstructions to be avoided in this zone". The table has a heading "Type of appliance" over its two right-hand columns, sub-headed "Turntable ladder dimension (m)" and "Hydraulic platform dimension (m)", and lists in its left column a. Maximum distance of near edge of hardstanding from building, b. Minimum width of hardstanding, c. Minimum distance of further edge of hardstanding from building, d. Minimum width of unobstructed space (for swing of appliance platform), with the values in metres (4.9/2.0; 5.0/5.5; 10.0/7.5; N/A/2.2). A "NOTES" heading introduces two numbered notes: 1. Hardstanding for high reach appliances should be as level as possible and should have a maximum gradient of 1 in 12. 2. Fire appliances are not standardised. Some fire services have appliances with a greater weight or different size. In consultation with the fire and rescue service, the building control body should adopt the relevant dimensions and ground loading capacity. A green caption at the bottom reads "Diagram 15.2 Relationship between building and hardstanding/access roads for high reach fire appliances".
